title: HandXFM: Semantic-Structural Distillation for Hand Radiograph Foundation Models
claim: A student encoder distilled from multiple frozen expert teachers with structure-aware masking becomes a universal encoder for many downstream tasks.
layout: 2 panels: large pretraining flow left-to-right, inset downstream heads bottom-right
description: A dense block diagram with two panels. Panel A, the large main area, shows three hand X-ray inputs on the left. The top one feeds a frozen expert image encoder (red trapezoid with snowflake), which produces red and yellow token columns. A Sobel edge branch makes an edge-aware mask. The middle input feeds the student encoder (blue trapezoid). The bottom input feeds HandXFM, which receives EMA updates from the student. Token columns are split into masked and visible indices and go to a mask regressor (green trapezoid). Arrows lead to the CLS, alignment, reconstruction and consistency loss boxes (orange and yellow) on the right. Panel B is a dashed inset at bottom right. It lists colored downstream heads (SvH, bone age, normal/abnormal, joint detection, segmentation, VQA) and a BiomedCLIP text encoder with text input. The eye goes first to the X-rays and the colored trapezoids.
caption: Overview of the proposed HandXFM framework. (A) Pretraining architecture. HandXFM jointly aligns the student encoder with multiple frozen medical experts while reconstructing masked latent features through the regressor. Edge-aware masking emphasizes structurally salient regions using Sobel gradients. The student learns from complementary objectives: multi-expert alignment loss, masked latent reconstruction loss, and EMA-based consistency loss, with an additional CLS-level supervision to preserve global semantics. (B) Downstream adaptation. After pretraining, the resulting foundation model serves as a universal encoder for diverse radiographic downstream tasks, including bone segmentation, joint detection, normal/abnormal classification, bone age prediction, SvH scoring, and VQA. The pretrained representation provides strong anatomical priors that transfer effectively across tasks and datasets.
abstract: Hand radiographs support diverse clinical tasks, including skeletal maturity assessment, rheumatoid arthritis scoring, abnormality screening, and anatomical localization, yet existing models are typically trained separately for each task and dataset. We present HandXFM, a domain-specific foundation model that leverages cross-modality knowledge for comprehensive hand X-ray understanding. HandXFM distills semantic priors from BiomedCLIP and structural cues from a chest X-ray Vision Transformer (ViT) through a unified alignment framework, integrating complementary medical knowledge in an interpretable way. After pretraining, HandXFM can be adapted to a range of musculoskeletal tasks, including bone age estimation, SvH score prediction, abnormality detection, joint localization, bone segmentation, and visual question answering. It consistently outperforms task-specific and single-expert baselines, achieving up to 0.11 improvement in Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) for bone age prediction and a 12\% accuracy gain in abnormality classification. Moreover, HandXFM generalizes to unseen datasets and yields cross-attention maps linking clinical terms to anatomical regions. These results demonstrate that multi-expert distillation effectively unifies semantic and structural supervision within a single pretrained model, establishing HandXFM as an interpretable and generalizable foundation model for hand radiograph analysis.
